Android accepted the lock, but the phone is on %1$s.
The modem is pinned to a specific cell.
The modem picks cells on its own.
Set over QMI first. If the modem refuses, Android network selection is used instead.
Uses Android\'s manual network selection, which stays after a reboot.
Locks LTE and NR to a PCI (the SA PCell or the NSA SCG). Leave the NR PCI empty to lock only the frequency, and separate several PCIs with commas.
Uses AT+EMMCHLCK, which holds one lock at a time. The PCI is optional, and the radio restarts to apply the lock.
This modem doesn\'t take AT+EMMCHLCK, so the frequency (ARFCN) is locked through the radio HAL instead. That can\'t lock to a PCI, and some modems ignore it.
Locks the frequency (ARFCN) through the radio HAL. This backend can\'t lock to a PCI, and some modems (stock Qualcomm, for example) only apply the band and ignore the channel.
